<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 60|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XXI.}}</noinclude>to IESVS they said, We know not. He also said to them, Neither do I tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=28}}† But vvhat is your opinion? A certaine man had tvvo sonnes: and comming to ‖ the first, he said, Sonne, goe vvorke to day in my vineyard. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=29}}† And he answering, said, I wil not. But aftervvard moued vvith repentance he vvent. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=30}}† And comming to the other, he said likevvise. And he ansvvering, said, I goe Lord, and he vvent not. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=31}}† VVhich of the tvvo did the fathers vvil? They say to him, The first. IESVS saith to them, Amē I say to you, that the Publicans and vvhoores goe before you into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=32}}† For Iohn came to you in the vvay of iustice: and you did not beleeue him. but the publicans and vvhoores did beleeue him: but you seeing it, neither haue ye had repentance aftervvard, to beleeue him.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=33}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon friday the second weeke in Lent.}}An other parable heare ye: A man there vvas an housholder vvho {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 5, 1. Mr. 12, 1. Lu. 20, 9.''}}* planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it, and digged in it a presse, and builded a tovvre, and let it out to husbandmen: and vvent forth into a strange countrie. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=34}}† And vvhen the time of fruites drevve nigh, he sent his seruants to the husbandmen, to receiue the fruites thereof. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=35}}† And the husbandmen apprehending his seruants, one they beat, an other they killed, and an other they stoned. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=36}}† Againe he sent other seruants moe then the former: and they did to them likevvise. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=37}}† And last of al he sent to them his sonne, saying, They vvil reuerence my sonne. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=38}}† But the husbandmen seeing the sonne, said vvithin them selues, This is the heire, come, let vs kil him, and vve shal haue his inheritaunce. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=39}}† And apprehending him they cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=40}}† When therfore the lord of the vineyard shal come, vvhat vvil he doe to those husbandmen? {{verse|chapter=21|verse=41}}† They say to him, The naughtie men he vvil bring to naught: and his vineyard he vvil let out to other husbandmen, that shal render him the fruite in their seasons.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=42}}† IESVS saith to them, Haue you neuer read in the Scriptures, ''The stone which the builders reiected, the same is made into the head of the corner? By our lord was this done, and it is maruelous in our eyes''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 117, 22.''}} {{verse|chapter=21|verse=43}}† Therfore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shal be taken avvay from you, and shal be giuen to a nation yelding the fruites thereof. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=44}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 8, 14.''}}* he that falleth vpon this stone, shal be broken: and on whom it falleth, it shal al to bruise him. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=45}}† And vvhen the cheefe Priestes and Pharisees had heard his parables, they knevve that he spake of them. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=46}}† And seeking<noinclude>{{rh|||to}}</noinclude>
